La documentación de esta integración la escribe su autor y, por ahora, solo está disponible en inglés.

This integration copies your **CalDAV** calendars (Google, iCloud, Nextcloud,
Fastmail, Infomaniak, Baïkal, Radicale, SOGo, Synology Calendar…) into the Gladys
calendar. The events show up in the calendar view, can trigger scenes ("an
event is coming") and are known by the assistant.

The sync is **one way**: Gladys reads your CalDAV server and never writes to
it. An event created or edited in Gladys on a synced calendar is not sent back
to the server.

## Enable the integration for your account

Every Gladys user enables the integration **for themselves**: your calendars
are personal data, nothing is synced until you enable it.

1. Open the **CalDAV** integration, **Configuration** tab.
2. In the **My calendars** block, fill in:
   - your **provider**: Google, iCloud, Fastmail and Infomaniak need no URL;
   - otherwise ("Other" provider), the **CalDAV server URL** (see the table
     below) — a URL typed here is always used, whatever the provider;
   - your **username**;
   - your **password** — use an **app password** when your provider offers
     one.
3. Click **Enable**. Your calendars show up a few seconds later.

| Provider   | Server URL                                          | Notes                                                         |
| ---------- | --------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Google     | in the list (`https://www.google.com/calendar/dav`) | Gmail address + app password (2-Step Verification must be on) |
| iCloud     | in the list (`https://caldav.icloud.com`)           | Apple ID + app-specific password (mandatory)                  |
| Fastmail   | in the list (`https://caldav.fastmail.com`)         | App password with CalDAV access                               |
| Infomaniak | in the list (`https://sync.infomaniak.com`)         | Infomaniak login (not the email address) + app password       |
| Nextcloud  | `https://cloud.example.com/remote.php/dav`          | App password: Settings → Security                             |
| Framagenda | `https://framagenda.org/remote.php/dav`             | App password: Settings → Security                             |
| Baïkal     | `https://dav.example.com/dav.php`                   |                                                               |
| Radicale   | `https://dav.example.com` (or `http://ip:5232`)     |                                                               |
| SOGo       | `https://mail.example.com/SOGo/dav`                 |                                                               |
| Synology   | `https://nas.example.com:5001/caldav`               |                                                               |

The integration discovers your calendars from that URL (principal and
calendar home): no need to enter the address of each calendar. Task lists are
ignored.

## Subscribed calendars (webcal)

The calendars your account is **subscribed** to by URL (public holidays,
sports fixtures, school timetable… — `webcal://` or `https://` addresses) are
synced too, when your server keeps the subscriptions in your account:
Nextcloud, iCloud, SOGo do. They show up in Gladys like your other calendars,
with the same toggles.

- The integration reads the feed **itself**, at its address: the feed must be
  reachable from your Gladys. It is read without your CalDAV credentials.
- A feed is read at every sync, but written to Gladys only when its content
  changed.
- A subscription that only exists in a client application (a calendar
  subscribed in Thunderbird or on a phone only) is not on the server: the
  integration cannot see it.

## Choose what to sync and share

Every synced calendar shows up in Gladys with two toggles:

- **Sync** — switch it off to skip a calendar: its events are removed from
  Gladys. Switched back on, it is refilled by the next sync.
- **Share** — a calendar starts **private**. Shared, it becomes visible to the
  whole household, and usable by the scenes.

The name, description and color of a calendar follow the server's.

## Settings (administrator)

These settings apply to every user:

- **Sync interval** — every 15 minutes by default (from 5 minutes to 24
  hours).
- **Days of history** — past events older than 30 days (by default) are not
  synced.
- **Days ahead** — 365 days by default (up to 730): recurring events are
  expanded up to that horizon.
- **Detailed logs** — off by default. Switched on, every CalDAV request and
  its result is written to the integration logs (see Troubleshooting).

The **Sync now** button reads every account right away and shows how many
calendars and events were synced.

## Good to know

- An event deleted on the server disappears from Gladys at the next sync; a
  calendar deleted on the server is deleted from Gladys with its events.
- Recurring events (exceptions and moved occurrences included) are expanded
  into individual occurrences.
- Cancelled events (`STATUS:CANCELLED`) are not imported.
- A "floating" time event (without time zone) is read as UTC.
- Gladys limits: 50 calendars per user (subscriptions included), 10,000
  events per calendar; texts too long are truncated.
- Disabling the integration for your account deletes your synced calendars
  from Gladys (they stay untouched on the server).

## Troubleshooting

The Configuration screen shows how many accounts fail. The most common
causes:

- **Wrong URL** — check the URL in a CalDAV client (Thunderbird, DAVx⁵); try
  the root URL of the server, the `/.well-known/caldav` discovery is
  automatic.
- **Credentials refused** — with two-factor authentication enabled, an app
  password is required.
- **Self-signed certificate** — the server must present a valid HTTPS
  certificate (or be reached over HTTP on the local network).
- **"N object(s) the server could not return were skipped"** — the server
  lists an event it then fails to send (Google does it on some calendars).
  The rest of the calendar is synced; only those objects are missing.
- **"feed …: 404 Not Found"** (or "not an iCalendar feed") — a subscribed
  calendar whose address no longer works: check it in your calendar
  application. The error names the feed's host only, its full address may
  hold a private key.

The administrator finds the details of the errors in the integration logs
(the integration page, supervision tab). Passwords never show up there.

To report a problem, switch on **Detailed logs** in the settings, click
**Sync now**, copy the logs, then switch the option off: they show each step
of the discovery and every request sent to the server, with the calendar
URLs (often your email address) — review them before posting them publicly.

## Parámetros de configuración

Estos son los parámetros que CalDAV te pide en su pantalla de configuración en Gladys.

| Parámetro | Tipo | Obligatorio | Descripción |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| How it works | `section` | No | Each user enables the integration for themselves in the "My calendars" block below, with their own CalDAV server and credentials. Their calendars and events are copied into Gladys, one way: Gladys never writes to the CalDAV server. The settings here apply to every user. |
| Sync interval (minutes) | `number` | No | How often each user's calendars are read from their CalDAV server. |
| Days of history | `number` | No | Past events older than this are not synced. |
| Days ahead | `number` | No | Horizon of the sync: recurring events are expanded up to this many days ahead. |
| Detailed logs | `boolean` | No | Writes every CalDAV request and its result to the integration logs, to diagnose a calendar that fails to sync. They hold the calendar URLs: switch it off once done. |

## Cómo instalar CalDAV en Gladys

1. En Gladys, abre **Integraciones**: CalDAV aparece en el catálogo junto a las integraciones nativas, con una insignia de comunidad.
2. Haz clic en **Instalar**. Gladys descarga la imagen Docker (`ghcr.io/bertrandda/gladys-caldav-sync:1.1.0`), la ejecuta en un entorno aislado del núcleo y genera la interfaz de la integración (dispositivos, descubrimiento y configuración).
3. Abre la pantalla de **Configuración** de la integración, rellena los parámetros y guarda.
4. También puedes instalarla directamente desde la URL de su repositorio: [https://github.com/bertrandda/gladys-caldav-sync](https://github.com/bertrandda/gladys-caldav-sync).

CalDAV requiere Gladys `>=5.2.0`. El catálogo de Gladys se actualiza cada hora, así que una nueva versión está disponible como máximo una hora después de publicarse.

¿Todavía no usas Gladys? Es gratuito y de código abierto: [sigue la guía de instalación](/es/docs/) para empezar.

## Sobre las integraciones externas

CalDAV es una **integración externa**: una integración comunitaria empaquetada como contenedor Docker y publicada en GitHub. Gladys la instala con un clic y la ejecuta en un entorno aislado del núcleo. La publica y mantiene [bertrandda](https://github.com/bertrandda), no el equipo principal de Gladys.
